sources.title: Talorys – A self-hosted personal AI agent on Cloudflare's free tier

editorial.how: According to the documentation: "The browser only ever talks to your .pages.dev site. /api/ requests run a Pages Function that forwards them over a service binding to the agent Worker. The agent Worker is deployed with workersdev: false and previewurls: false: it has no public URL. Authentication and authorization happen in the Worker, not the frontend. Chat responses stream as Server-Sent Events end-to-end."
editorial.why: The GitHub API reports 1k stars and 91 forks, 5 days after the repository was created. It gained 116 stars across 52 hours of our snapshots. Primary language: TypeScript.
editorial.what: Your personal AI agent in your own Cloudflare account. Chat, memory, tasks, notes and scheduled reminders, deployed with one command: npx create-talorys@latest. Free-tier friendly, single-user, no telemetry. From the documentation: "Talorys is a free, open-source personal AI assistant that runs entirely inside your own Cloudflare account. It chats with you, remembers what matters, manages tasks, notes and projects, and runs reminders and routines on a schedule — without any server, database or account operated by the Talorys developers."
editorial.whoCares: Developers building or operating agents that use tools, browsers or computers.
limitations: One independent reference so far: Hacker News.

GreenWAM: A World Foundation Model for Robotics

editorial.how: We present GreenWAM, a world foundation model for robotics, together with the recipe that produces it: (1) a shared anatomical action space that describes 20 robot families, from bimanual arms to dexterous humanoids, in common joint coordinates; (2) joint training on these families in visual, action-conditioned and world-action modes; and (3) policies that split an action expert off the generator.
editorial.why: No distinguishing evidence has been collected yet beyond the listing itself.
editorial.what: A robot needs a world model that predicts how its actions will change the scene and a policy that chooses those actions. Models are usually built and evaluated for only one of these roles, and every robot records its actions in its own format. We ask whether one robot world model can serve both roles across different bodies, and what makes this work. We present GreenWAM, a world foundation model for robotics,…
editorial.whoCares: Robotics engineers and researchers working on embodied systems.
limitations: One independent reference so far: Hugging Face Papers.
Preprint: not peer reviewed.
